Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5543; inefficient, i.e. (by implication) detrimental:--unprofitable.
BiblicalUsage: Unprofitable — achrestos appears once, in Paul's letter about Onesimus: "Which in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me." A runaway slave, useless to his master, has become useful — to Philemon, and to Paul.
TheologicalSignificance: A single verse about a runaway slave carries no doctrine in the adjective, and the gospel in the verse is that grace made the useless man useful.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
